titleEn: While We Wait, Play the Raindrops!

pages.text: "When will the rain stop?" Mumu stamped beneath the eaves. Water streamed from their edge. Today, the friends had planned to visit the stream.
"I want to dip my feet in!" Quick-handed monkey Taro reached beyond the eaves. "The rain's still heavy. Let's go when it stops."
Mumu sat, stood, then sat again. "I'm bored. It's no fun." With drooping ears, Mumu leaned against a post.
Taro lined up three coconut shells beneath the eaves. Drops fell differently into each. Tong, tok, tik.
"Hear that? Three different sounds." Taro tapped the shells twice with a branch. Mumu's ears turned toward them. "While We Wait, Play the Raindrops!"
Mumu moved one shell a little sideways. Its sound changed from tok to tong. "That makes it louder!"
They took turns moving the shells. Tong-tong, tok-tok, tik-tik. Mumu bounded to the rain's rhythm. "While We Wait, Play the Raindrops!"
Soon, Mumu was no longer stamping. "Rain, you can stay a little longer." Smiling, Mumu sat before the shells.
Mumu watched the rain beyond the eaves. "One, play with what's here! Two, look for sounds! Three, take turns!" Taro added another shell.
The rain grew lighter, then stopped. Taro leaned snugly against Mumu's back. Waiting had not felt long at all. Looking toward the yard, they called, "While We Wait, Play the Raindrops!"
